'''Jalen Derale Wilson''' (born November 4, 2000)<ref>{{cite web |title=Jalen Wilson |url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Jalen-Wilson/B12/University-of-Kansas/420988 |work=US Basket |access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. He was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] his junior year.<ref>{{cite news |last=DeCourcy |first=Mike |date=March 7, 2023 |title=Sporting News 2022-23 college basketball All-America team |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2022-23-college-basketball-all-america-team/ynhqsffrvax9novxmglr2fgo |access-date=March 7, 2023 |work=[[Sporting News]]}}</ref>

==High school career==
Wilson attended [[John H. Guyer High School]] in [[Denton, Texas]]. As a junior, he averaged 16.1 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game. As a senior, he averaged 18.1 points, 7.5 rebounds and three assists per game, earning Class 6A All-State honors.<ref>{{cite web |last=Galloway |first=Matt |date=June 12, 2019 |title=Bill Self: Newest KU basketball signee Jalen Wilson to bring 'incredible toughness' |url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/20190612/bill-self-newest-ku-basketball-signee-jalen-wilson-to-bring-incredible-toughness |access-date=January 12, 2021 |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]]}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Wilson was a consensus four-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the 46th-best player in the 2019 class by [[247Sports]]. He originally committed to playing college basketball for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] but reopened his recruitment with the departure of head coach [[John Beilein]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hoyt |first=Joseph |title=Denton Guyer's Jalen Wilson requests release from Michigan days after John Beilein heads to Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2019/05/16/denton-guyer-s-jalen-wilson-requests-release-from-michigan-days-after-john-beilein-heads-to-cleveland-cavaliers/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=May 16, 2019}}</ref> He later committed to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] over an offer from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gosset |first=Brian |title=From one basketball power to another: Guyer 4-star SF Jalen Wilson is headed to Big 12 |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/article231482188.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=June 12, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 8, 2019, Wilson suffered a broken ankle against [[UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball|UNC Greensboro]] in his second career game. He missed the remainder of the season and was granted a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] after undergoing surgery.<ref>{{cite web |last=Blen |first=Max |title='I've been waiting a long time': New look Jalen Wilson is ready to play again for KU |url=https://www.kansan.com/sports/i-ve-been-waiting-a-long-time-new-look-jalen-wilson-is-ready-to-play/article_42a49bc4-2cfe-11eb-b1cc-7360e76bf5f1.html |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> On December 8, 2020, Wilson recorded 23 points and 10 rebounds, making a go-ahead three-pointer with 42 seconds remaining, in a 73–72 win over eighth-ranked [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Skretta |first=Dave |title=Wilson hits go-ahead 3 in closing seconds as Kansas defeats Creighton 73-72 |url=https://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/jalen-wilson-go-ahead-3-pointer-kansas-jayhawks-win-creighton-bluejays-120820 |website=Fox Sports |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=December 8, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, Wilson averaged 11.8 points and 7.9 rebounds per game, earning [[Big 12]] All-Freshman Team honors. On April 9, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lance |first=Sam |date=April 9, 2021 |title=Jalen Wilson declares for 2021 NBA Draft, will retain eligibility |url=https://www.kansan.com/sports/jalen-wilson-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-will-retain-eligibility/article_2c7b9df0-9970-11eb-b82d-b3c440eae776.html |access-date=May 30, 2021 |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]]}}</ref> Wilson ultimately returned to Kansas. On November 2, he was suspended for three games due to an arrest on suspicion of DUI.<ref>{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=November 2, 2021 |title=Kansas' Jalen Wilson suspended 3 regular-season games following DUI arrest |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32535533 |access-date=November 3, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Wilson was named to the third-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite news |last=Swain |first=Michael |date=March 6, 2022 |title=Ochai Agbaji named Big 12 POY as five other Jayhawks earn conference honors |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-Big-12-Player-of-the-Year-KU-basketball-All-Big-12-teams-Christian-Braun-David-McCormack-Jalen-Wilson-183978357/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307004932/https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-Big-12-Player-of-the-Year-KU-basketball-All-Big-12-teams-Christian-Braun-David-McCormack-Jalen-Wilson-183978357/ |archive-date=March 7, 2022 |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=247Sports}}</ref> He averaged 11.1 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, helping the Jayhawks win a national title. Following the season Wilson declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] but ultimately withdrew from the draft.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tait |first=Matt |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Kansas forward Jalen Wilson withdraws from NBA draft, will return to KU for 2022-23 season |url=https://www2.kusports.com/news/2022/jun/01/kansas-forward-jalen-wilson-withdraws-nba-draft-wi/ |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=[[Kansas Jayhawks]]}}</ref> As a junior, Wilson was named [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]].<ref name="Big12awards">{{cite press release |title=Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced |date=March 5, 2023 |publisher=Big 12 Conference |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2023/3/5/phillips-66-all-big-12-mens-basketball-awards-announced.aspx |access-date=March 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2026)===
Wilson was selected by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with the 51st overall pick in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Denton Guyer's Jalen Wilson selected by Brooklyn Nets in 2nd round of NBA draft|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2023/06/22/denton-guyers-jalen-wilson-selected-by-brooklyn-nets-in-2nd-round-of-nba-draft/|work=Dallas News|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=December 30, 2023}}</ref> On July 5, 2023, Wilson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 5, 2023 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Jalen Wilson to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-jalen-wilson-to-two-way-contract |access-date=July 5, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>  On December 27, Wilson recorded his first double double, scoring a career-high 21 points and grabbing ten rebounds in a 144-122 loss to the [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nets fall 144-122 to Bucks as starters rest, reserves put up fight |url=https://sny.tv/articles/nets-bucks-recap-12-27-23 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=sny.tv}}</ref> On March 1, 2024, the Brooklyn Nets converted Wilson's two-way contract to a standard multi-year NBA contract.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 1, 2024 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Jalen Wilson to Multi-Year Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-jalen-wilson-to-multi-year-contract |access-date=March 1, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made 43 appearances (including three starts) for Brooklyn as a rookie, averaging 5.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.0 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jalen Wilson 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431714/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Wilson made 79 appearances (including 22 starts) for the Nets during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 9.5 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jalen Wilson 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431714/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He played in 54 games (starting two) for Brooklyn in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 6.4 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jalen Wilson 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431714/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks / College Park Skyhawks (2026–present)===
On July 20, 2026, Wilson signed a two–way contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hawks Sign Former Nets Forward Jalen Wilson to Two-Way Deal|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/hawks-sign-former-nets-forward-030431871.html|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>
